question: In the reference of Constitution of India, who, was the elected president of the Constituent Assembly from following?
solution:
The correct answer is __Rajendra Prasad__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The Constituent Assembly was formed for the creation of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Constituent Assembly was formed in July 1946 based on the recommendations of the Cabinet Mission.
 
• As a prominent leader of congress, Dr. Rajendra Prasad worked with Mahatma Gandhi and other leaders.
 
• Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the President of the Constituent Assembly.
 
• Dr. Rajendra Prasad worked as the longest-serving President of India (1950 to 1962).
 
• Rajendra Prasad was elected as the first President of India on 24th January 1950 and the vice-president was Harendra Coomar Mookerjee.
 
• He was one of the prominent leaders of the Indian independence movement and played a prominent role as the President of the Indian National Congress. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• B. R. Ambedkar was an Indian polytheist, economist, politician, and social reformer.

 
 
• After the independence of India, he became the first Law and Justice Minister of independent India.
 
• He was the father of the Indian Constitution and one of the architects of the Republic of India.
 
• He was the chairman of the Drafting Committee.
 
 
 
• Lal Bahadur Shastri was born on 2nd October in 1904 at Mughalsarai, Uttar Pradesh in a simple family.
 
 
• His father name was Mr. Sharada Prasad and his mother name was Mrs. Ramdulari Devi. His father died when he was only a year old. 
 
• He got his education from the East Central Railway Inter College in the Mughalsarai, Varanasi.
 
• He had joined the non-cooperation movement against British Government in 1921 by Mahatma Gandhi when he was only seventeen years old. 
 
• He had completed his graduation from the Kashi Vidyapeeth, Varanasi in the year 1926 and was awarded the title of Shastri.
 
• On 11 January 1966, he died in Tashkent, USSR (now Uzbekistan) after signing the Tashkent Declaration with Pakistani President Ayub Khan.
 
 
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was born on 14 November 1889 in Allahabad.
 
 
• In 1912, he participated in the Bankipur Conference as a delegate.
 
• In 1919, he became the Secretary of the Home Rule League of Allahabad.
 
• In 1916, he met Mahatma Gandhi for the first time, from whom he was greatly inspired.
 
• He is the first prime minister of India.
